audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer was described as an 'E shield-break' in three places, and Neeko's ult setup was credited to 'W-invis' twice.
audit.why: Riot's text: Sion's E damages, slows and reduces ARMOR of the first enemy hit, and knocks a struck minion backwards through everyone behind it — it does not break shields. His shield is W, Soul Furnace, which he can reactivate after 3s for damage. Neeko's Shapesplitter is a directional clone with a third-attack proc; what hides the Pop Blossom preparation is Inherent Glamour's disguise.
audit.corrected: E named as armour shred plus minion knockback, W named as the shield, and the ult setup credited to the disguise.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff FAVOURED at 4/10 on a lane sitting at exactly 50% over 26 games, whose own chart splits four rows even.
audit.why: 50% with a Sion/Skill/Skill/Skill/Neeko/Neeko/Sion chart is an even lane, not a favoured one. Both layers already agree with the packet chart, so no rows were touched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ item spike said only that he gets tanky and keeps fighting after death; nothing told you what to buy about it.
audit.why: Glory in Death makes his post-death attacks heal him and deal max-health damage, and Soul Furnace grows his max HP off kills — missingInteractions lists both needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Late spike now names Glory in Death's healing and calls for Grievous Wounds by then.

edits.before: Sion's charged Q and his E shield-break are the whole early game — at level 1 you have no combo and only single-target Q value, so don't trade into his E poke or stand where a full Q knockup catches you. Farm with the edge of Blooming Burst and respect that he wins the raw stat-check. Once you hit 3 you get a real window: a landed Tangle-Barbs roots an immobile Sion, and you can stack Q re-blooms on him before he charges anything back. Never throw E into minions — wait for a clean line.
edits.after: Decimating Smash and Roar of the Slayer are the whole early game — the charged Q knocks up, the E slows and shreds your armour, and at level 1 you have no combo and single-target Q value, so do not trade into it. Farm with the edge of Blooming Burst and accept he wins the raw stat-check. At 3 you get a real window: a landed Tangle-Barbs roots an immobile Sion and you stack Q re-blooms before he charges anything back. Careful throwing E through minions — his E knocks one back through you.

edits.before: Level 6 is where this flips your way. Pop Blossom turns a landed E into a burst-stun combo, and his immobility means he cannot dodge your root or escape the channel once it lands — use disguise or W-invis to start the ult unseen so he can't pre-fire his charged Q to knock you out of it. The danger is exactly that: a full-charge Q interrupts your wind-up, so stun him with R after the root, not before. Force your trades on his Q cooldown and during your first-item spike.
edits.after: Level 6 is where this flips your way. Pop Blossom turns a landed E into a burst-stun combo, and his immobility means he cannot dodge the root or leave once it lands — stay disguised so the preparation is hidden and he cannot pre-fire a charged Q at your wind-up. That is the danger exactly: a full-charge knockup catches you mid-preparation, so root first and R second, never the other way. Force trades on his 10s Q cooldown and during your first-item spike.

edits.before: Hit your level 6 and use disguise/W-invis to set up R unseen for a surprise stun-combo
edits.after: Hit level 6 and stay disguised so the R preparation stays hidden until the stun lands
